source: md/1_PRD.md FR-12 (line 184: 'Assign to committee/member by Region and workload, with conflict-of-interest declaration') and PRD §19 Appendix E (line 412: 'Proposed fields: declaration, type, timestamp, reviewer, exclusion, reassignment. Do not claim COI handling exists without approved policy and tests'). The PRD names workload balancing and a COI declaration as requirements but defines neither a workload formula nor a conflict rule — both are open, so they ship as clearly-labelled placeholder configuration (the same pattern as the 3.3 stage-limit day counts and the 3.4 escalation ladder).
note: PLACEHOLDER ASSIGNMENT POLICY — FR-12 requires assignment 'by Region and workload, with conflict-of-interest declaration', but the PRD defines no workload formula and no conflict rule, and Appendix E explicitly says COI handling must not be claimed 'without approved policy and tests'. So both halves ship as clearly-labelled placeholder configuration: AICTE must confirm the workload-balancing formula and what actually constitutes a conflict before any of it is treated as Unverified. Workload balancing only reorders who gets a case among officers the route + jurisdiction already allow — it never grants access to an officer whose jurisdiction does not cover the case. COI is ADVISORY and HIDING only (DEC-0003): a declared, unresolved conflict hides the case from that officer and keeps them out of the assignment pool; it never gates, moves, blocks or rejects a case, and a workflow action is never refused because someone declared a COI.

workload.soft_max_note: PLACEHOLDER — no PRD figure exists for a per-officer caseload cap. 10 is a project proposal, not an AICTE rule. Advisory only: the assignment pool still includes an officer above the soft max (they are simply ordered last), so a queue is never left empty because everyone is 'busy'. AICTE must confirm the real cap before this is trusted.
workload.source: PRD FR-12 line 184: 'by Region and workload'. The PRD names workload as a factor but defines no formula and no cap, so this is a labelled placeholder.

conflict_of_interest.note: The PRD (Appendix E) proposes a COI schema but explicitly says not to claim COI handling exists without an approved policy. So this prototype RECORDS a declaration and HIDES the case from the declarer — the minimum honest behaviour — but does NOT apply an automatic conflict *rule* (it does not guess that same-region or same-institution is a conflict). The types below are the declaration vocabulary; the decision of what counts as a conflict stays with a human reviewer, exactly as Appendix E describes (reviewer, exclusion, reassignment).

conflict_of_interest.effect_note: A declared, unresolved COI HIDES the case from the declarer (they are skipped in assignment and excluded from an assigned-scoped officer's visible list) and keeps them out of the workload pool. It is advisory and never gates: the case still moves through the workflow, and a human reviewer decides the exclusion/reassignment (Appendix E). Resolving or revoking a declaration restores visibility.
